_note: HANDOFF's UEMOA NCOA retarget pass (opened round 6, lead in round5-little-things-2026-09-06.json's own _dropped: 'bf-insd-ihpc / other UEMOA IHPC releases -> afristat-ncoa-ihpc'). Read each remaining UEMOA member's OWN current bulletin (Burkina Faso, Benin, Mali, Guinea-Bissau — Senegal, Niger, Côte d'Ivoire already correctly wired to un-coicop-2018 per the same lead's vintage-split note, and Togo already wired to uemoa-reg-2024-base2023) rather than inferring from AFRISTAT's guide, per rule 3. Finding differs from the lead's own framing: none of the four countries' current bulletins name a 'NCOA 2018' edition the way Senegal's does — all four still label their classification table simply 'NCOA-IHPC' (Guinea-Bissau's own footnote glosses it as 'Nomenclatura de Consumo Oeste Africana', no year), so retargeting them to afristat-ncoa-ihpc (a node whose own description explicitly says it is the PRE-2018 vintage) would be exactly the edition-by-inference the corpus's own IMTS-Revision-2 refusal exists to stop. Recorded as `deferred` below rather than minted. What every one of the four DOES self-declare, cleanly, is the base-2023 transition itself: each country's own current bulletin states in its own preliminary-information section that its IHPC/INHPC is now base 100 = 2023, replacing/renovating from base 2014, as part of the common eight-member UEMOA methodology — which is exactly what `uemoa-reg-2024-base2023` (currently wired only from Togo, at C, off the regulation's own binding text rather than a national self-citation) asserts. Four new SELF-DECLARED edges to that node, one per country, all fetched live 2026-09-08 (the corpus's stored URLs for three of the four were stale: Benin's was an archived 2016 bulletin, Guinea-Bissau's afristat-ihpc-guide-2014 edge cited a 2024 edition, Burkina Faso's own node URL happened to already be current). Graded B, not A: each self-declares the base-2023 renovation plainly, but the target's own title is a regulation title ('Règlement N°05/2024/CM/UEMOA... (IHPC base 100 en 2023)'), not the guide's own plain name, and none of the four quotes below names the regulation by number — the same shape that kept Togo's edge at C, just self-declared rather than register-sourced this time, which is the one thing rule 19 says to prefer even at the same grade.

_dropped.why: The round-6 lead (round5-little-things-2026-09-06.json _dropped) proposed retargeting these four (plus the other nine already resolved onto un-coicop-2018 or left as-is) onto afristat-ncoa-ihpc once minted. Now read: all four countries' current bulletins (fetched live 2026-09-08) do label their classification table 'NCOA-IHPC', but NONE states an edition year the way Senegal's base-2023 bulletin explicitly says 'NCOA 2018' -- Guinea-Bissau's own footnote only glosses the acronym ('Nomenclatura de Consumo Oeste Africana'), no date. afristat-ncoa-ihpc's own description states it is the PRE-2018 vintage, superseded for the current base-2023 series -- exactly the edition inference the corpus's IMTS-Revision-2 refusal (round 5's other _dropped entry, same file) exists to block: reading '2018' or 'pre-2018' onto a document that states neither is the researcher's inference, not the document's statement. Deferred rather than minted; the four all got a different, better-evidenced edge instead (-> uemoa-reg-2024-base2023, same slice). Re-open only if a document surfaces that states which NCOA-IHPC edition (2008/2014-era vs. 2018) each country's current base-2023 series actually runs on.
